domain: Historical Sociology / State Formation / Commitment Systems
topic_summary: Analysis of Meiji Japan's top-down imposition of Gregorian calendar and Western dress codes as a test case for commitment system vocabulary. The kernel question: did the new reading displace the prior one through endogenous climb (gradual adoption from fringe) or exogenous override (state-imposed replacement)? This tests whether the M-set framework's absence of a 'top-down imposition' cell represents a structural gap or correct exclusion.

key_entities: Meiji State (centralizing authority imposing Western calendar/dress)
key_tensions: State modernization imperative vs embedded temporal/sartorial practice
Top-down imposition vs endogenous adoption pathways
key_mechanisms: Legal mandate (calendar change enforced by decree, 1873)
Institutional requirement (Western dress required for government/military personnel)
Symbolic legitimation (Western forms as markers of civilization/modernity)
key_absences: M-set framework lacks cell for exogenous top-down imposition as distinct from endogenous climb

omegas.description: Does the M-set framework's lack of a top-down imposition cell represent a structural gap (the framework cannot handle exogenous override) or correct exclusion (all apparent overrides are actually compressed climbs with invisible fringe adoption)? The Meiji case tests this directly.

Did calendar/dress changes persist because of continued enforcement or because they became self-sustaining commitments? If the former, they remain state-dependent scaffolds; if the latter, they transitioned to mountains or ropes.

Were there invisible fringe adopters (e.g., merchant class, treaty port residents) whose pre-decree adoption the historical record does not capture? If so, the 'top-down' imposition may be a compressed climb misread as override.

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Kernel decomposition applied as specified. State capacity threshold identified as independent mountain axis.

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The pathway by which a new commitment reading displaces a prior one — whether through endogenous adoption from fringe (climb) or exogenous state imposition (override)
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: State authority to mandate temporal and sartorial practice; legitimacy grounded in modernization imperative and international standing

readings.commitment: All commitment displacement occurs through fringe adoption and gradual climb; apparent top-down impositions are compressed climbs with invisible fringe stages
readings.authority_grounding: M-set framework as currently specified (no top-down cell)
readings.expected_structural_delta: Meiji calendar/dress changes had pre-decree fringe adoption (treaty ports, merchant class, military modernizers); state decree accelerated but did not initiate; enforcement was ratification of existing climb

readings.commitment: State capacity enables commitment displacement without fringe adoption pathway; top-down imposition is a distinct mechanism requiring separate M-set cell
readings.authority_grounding: Historical sociology of state formation; Weberian state capacity theory
readings.expected_structural_delta: Meiji calendar/dress changes had no meaningful pre-decree fringe adoption; state decree created new commitment through enforcement; compliance was coerced, not emergent; M-set framework incomplete without override cell

readings.commitment: Top-down imposition creates artificial fringe (state employees, military) which then climbs organically; override initiates, climb completes
readings.authority_grounding: Institutional diffusion theory; two-stage adoption models
readings.expected_structural_delta: Meiji decree created mandatory fringe (government/military personnel required to adopt); this artificial fringe then became organic climb vector; M-set framework captures this as compressed climb with state-manufactured fringe

axiom_contradictions.basis: Endogenous climb reading holds that all commitment displacement requires fringe adoption as necessary precondition; exogenous override reading holds that state capacity can bypass fringe adoption entirely. No single framework can hold both axioms — accepting override as distinct mechanism requires rejecting climb as universal pathway.
